transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Martinez (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cascade ML, CTO), Rafiq Khan (ML Engineer), Sofia Alvarez (Infra), Jon (Finance)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery focused on model selection and deployment mode. Primary needs: long context (30-64k), multilingual support (EN/ES/FR/DE/APAC languages), reliable function/tool calling for retrieval and db lookups, and clear security posture for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 

I'm Lena, I'm the AE on the account, Owen is our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi I'm Maya, CTO at Cascade. We build a document understanding product for legal + finance, lots of long docs, multilingual.
[00:14] Rafiq Khan: Rafiq here, ML eng, I'm focused on latency and cost, also model accuracy across Spanish/Portuguese.
[00:20] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, infra lead, I'll own networking/VPC questions.
[00:24] Jon: Jon from finance, here to listen on cost/pricing.
[00:28] Lena: Great. We usually start with current stack  can you walk us through how you're doing extraction today and what you want to improve?
[00:36] Maya: Sure. Right now we host an ensemble of open models on GCP, mostly llama2 variants and a few finetuned checkpoints, plus a retrieval step. But latency is all over, and cost spikes when customers upload 30k+ token docs. We also need better tool-calling for structured extraction  calling our internal DB or running a risk-scoring microservice.
[00:55] Owen: Got it. Are you measuring tokens-per-inference currently or just latency p95?
[00:59] Rafiq: We track both, but tokens-per-inference is noisy because of caching variations. Latency p95 target we'd like under 700ms for typical 2k token outputs, but for longer context it's obviously higher.
[01:12] Lena: And desired context window? You mentioned 30k.
[01:15] Maya: Ideally 32k, but some enterprise customers ask for 64k for whole-deal docs. We'll probably pilot with 32k, then evaluate 64k.
[01:22] Owen: For 32k you can use certain open models and tuned quantization profiles, but there's a tradeoff on latency/cost  that's where Redwood caching + batching helps. We also support automatic prefix/KV cache to avoid reprocessing repeated context.
[01:36] Rafiq: How well do open models do on Spanish/Portuguese? We tried a few off-the-shelf Llama 2 variants and quality drops on legal Spanish.
[01:44] Owen: Multilingual performance varies. Mistral-ish models and a few community multilingual checkpoints can be decent, but you might need finetuning or instruction-tuning on your corpus. Redwood focuses on serving and giving recommendations  our Optimize tooling can suggest model + quantization combos based on your workload.
[01:57] Maya: We care about function calling  our pipeline needs the model to call a function to fetch contract metadata then populate structured fields. Does Redwood hosted support tool-calling / function-calls?
[02:07] Lena: Yes  hosted supports streaming, function-calling patterns and structured outputs. For privacy-sensitive customers we often recommend Dedicated or Private where you can control network egress and KMS.
[02:17] Sofia: On private, what's the difference between Dedicated and Private? We need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS, maybe air-gapped later.
[02:25] Owen: Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools in our infra with capacity guarantees and isolation. Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane (VPC/on-prem options) and can be configured to use your KMS/HSM, tighter audit logs, and no shared tenancy. If you need air-gapped, that's in Private.
[02:40] Maya: SOC2 and ISO?
[02:42] Lena: We have SOC2 Type II and are pursuing ISO; we'll send the security whitepaper after the call.
[02:48] Jon: Cost wise, what should we expect for 32k context vs 8k? Our CFO will want ballpark numbers.
[02:55] Owen: It depends on model and batching. For hosted open models, per-token unit cost is lower but you share infrastructure. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latencies for heavy workloads. We will send a hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet with examples of 8k/32k scenarios.
[03:08] Rafiq: Latency targets  you mentioned batching can increase latency. How do you balance throughput vs p95?
[03:14] Owen: Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching and dynamic routing; you can set SLOs (latency or cost). For strict p95 you tune for lower batching and possibly higher instance count; for cost efficiency we recommend adaptive batching plus prefix cache for repeated documents.
[03:29] Maya: For model selection we need an apples-to-apples benchmark on our prompt sets. Can Redwood run side-by-side on our dataset?
[03:36] Lena: Absolutely. Owen can run a benchmark with two candidate models (one strong multilingual 32k model, one cost-efficient 8k model) on your prompt set. We'll include latency, cost, and quality metrics.
[03:47] Owen: Quick note: some transcription stuff  the KV cache sometimes gets transcribed as K-V cash in our notes, just FYI.
[03:53] (laughter)
[03:55] Rafiq: Any specific open models you recommend for long-context legal docs? We tried a community 70B model but memory was brutal.
[04:02] Owen: There are a couple of long-context variants (longform Llama forks, some Mistral community builds). Also consider models with explicit attention-window optimizations. Redwood's model catalog tags models by verified context length and performance profile. We often recommend a 2-model strategy for pilots: 1) high-quality long-context model (32k) for fidelity; 2) smaller, quantized model for low-cost autoscaling.
[04:24] Maya: Tooling: we need function-calls to both call our retrieval service and an internal scoring service (runs in 120ms). Does Redwood support custom tool adapters?
[04:33] Owen: Yes, we support function/tool calling patterns and you can wire adapters via the API. For Dedicated/Private we can also allow network rules so calls stay inside your network or go to your internal proxies.
[04:43] Sofia: VPC peering and egress  will you let us push logs to our SIEM and integrate with our KMS?
[04:50] Lena: With Private you can manage KMS and push logs; Dedicated supports S3-compatible log export and audit trails, and we have integrations for common SIEMs. We'll include the audit log sample in the security pack.
[05:02] Jon: Timeline  if we do a pilot, how long to stand up Dedicated or Private?
[05:07] Owen: Hosted is immediate. Dedicated typically takes a couple of weeks for capacity + networking settings; Private depends on on-prem needs but initial VPC-style deployments can be in a few weeks with proper scoping. We'll need to scope networking, certs, and KMS.
[05:20] Maya: Ok. For the benchmark, can you run 8k vs 32k and include multilingual evals? We'll send a Spanish/Portuguese subset.
[05:28] Owen: Yes, we'll plan for that. Also we'll surface recommended quantization and model variant for each SLA.
[05:35] (brief crosstalk, background noise)
[05:40] Rafiq: Security question  data retention for hosted; we may need option to disable retention and purge logs.
[05:47] Lena: Hosted supports configurable retention and data controls; for customers needing strict controls we recommend Dedicated or Private where you can fully control persisting data.
[05:55] Maya: Anything else we should be aware of?
[05:58] Owen: One operational note  when using very long contexts, memory and KV cache behavior can cause tokenization edge cases; we'll include some guidance and a checklist in the benchmark packet.
[06:10] Lena: Great. Recap + next steps: Lena to send pricing + security docs, Owen to run benchmark plan and perf spreadsheet, Maya to share prompt sets. Schedule scoping call for Private if infra wants it.
[06:22] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:25] Lena: Thanks, we'll follow up.

(End of transcript)

Notes: occasional small transcription errors (product names, KV cache as K-V cash). References shared: benchmark spreadsheet (link provided in follow-up), SOC2 whitepaper (link), hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet (to be sent).
